description: The Urban Model Platform is open source software that gives access to existing analysis and simulation models from science, administration and business, so that planners can test decisions on building, traffic, climate and resilience before they are made. It was developed by the City Science Lab of HafenCity University Hamburg with the Hamburg Agency for Geoinformation and Surveying (LGV) in the Connected Urban Twins project. Written in Python, it works as a system of systems: models stay on the servers of their owners and are exposed through one central address with a standard interface, the OGC API Processes, so that simulations and their results can be built into different user interfaces. It runs in containers, including Kubernetes, and supports OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 for secure runs across organisations. Hamburg operates the platform and offers services on it; the Scenario Explorer, built on Masterportal, drives UMP analyses such as a noise simulation. The code is free on GitHub; the licence is given in the repository, not on the page. Caveats: the page and examples are in German, and the page notes that the demo noise simulation uses simplified assumptions. Coverage is Hamburg, Germany, with reuse by other cities intended. It supports digital twin and model coupling work for urban infrastructure; the related record is the Connected Urban Twins resources.
